content.text:
I read the transcript and the record, matched each key item to the record item that captures it, and checked every figure, owner and date against the final version agreed in the meeting.

**Pairing summary**

- **e1** → record 3 ("last day at Grevholm 2026-09-25"). Record 4 restates the same job change from the other side, so it counts as a split of the same life event rather than a second key item.
- **e2** → record 1 ("Relocation to Tennessee for work"). No figures, so nothing to get wrong; the lease terms are simply absent.
- **e3** (Woodbury sale, $604,000, Oct 30 close, $353,800 net) → nothing in the record.
- **e4** (Graham's remote approval from Tollefsrud) → nothing in the record as a life event.
- **a1** → record 5, correctly carrying $387,240, the *vested* balance Renata read out mid-meeting, not the $430,000 she guessed first. This is the one figure the record gets exactly right.
- **a2** (house account + $340,000 four-rung T-bill ladder) → no account action; record 7 is the Jules task, which belongs to i6.
- **a3** and **a4** → nothing. The standing no-gains hold Hollis placed before the meeting is entirely missing.
- **i2** → record 8: right owner (reassigned to Jules because Hollis is out Sept 21–25), but the due date is wrong. "End of next week" from a Sept 15 meeting is Friday Sept 25, 2026; the record encodes 2026-10-27, which contradicts its own task text.
- **i3** → record 6: Graham, before October 1. Encoding the deadline as 2026-10-01 is consistent with "before the first".
- **i6** → record 7: Jules, 2026-10-23, derived correctly after Graham corrected the closing from "the thirteenth" to October 30.
- **i7** → record 9: right owner and scope, but Renata committed to doing it *tonight*, September 15, because the draft pulls on the 1st. A due date of 2026-10-01 is the deadline she was told to beat, not the date agreed.
- **i1, i4, i5** → absent: no rollover paperwork task for Jules (due moved from Friday Sept 18 to Tuesday Oct 6), no Venholt deferral task, no TN license/voter/car registration task.

**Declined and deferred items:** none of the six leaked into the record — no Roth conversion, no 529 transfer, no allocation change, no COBRA, no cabin, no backdoor Roth.

**Problem item:** record 2, "Purchase of a new house in Tennessee," is materially wrong. They signed a 12-month lease at $4,150; a purchase is twelve to eighteen months out and explicitly not part of the plan.

key_items.note: Captures the Grevholm departure with the correct last day 2026-09-25. Comp details ($265,000 base, $40,000 sign-on repayable within 12 months, $15,000 moving lump sum, $42,760 forfeited profit-sharing) and the VP of distribution operations title are omitted, but no figure is stated wrongly. Record 4 covers the other half of the same job change and is treated as a split.

'Relocation to Tennessee for work' captures the family move. Missing the Woodbury-to-Franklin detail, the 12-month lease at $4,150/month from October 1, the October 1 residency date and the October 5 school start, but carries no incorrect figure.

No record item covers the Woodbury home sale: under contract at $604,000, mail-away close Friday October 30, estimated net $353,800, ~$128,000 gain fully covered by the $500,000 exclusion. Record 2 concerns a Tennessee purchase, not this sale.

Graham's fully remote approval from Tollefsrud Mutual (Minneapolis), keeping his job with two or three days a quarter in Minneapolis, is not recorded as a life event. Record 6 is the separate payroll action item (i3) and cannot also serve here.

Correctly uses $387,240, the vested balance Renata read out, rather than the $430,000 total she first estimated, and names Ferrant Custody. Does not spell out 'direct rollover' or 'new Rollover IRA managed by Kessling Marrow', but the substance and the figure are right.

No account action for the joint house account funded by the title company wire (~$353,800) with $340,000 into a 3/6/9/12-month T-bill ladder of four $85,000 rungs and the remainder in money market. Record 7 is the i6 task (open account, send wire instructions by Oct 23) and is paired there.
No account action recording the pause of the $2,000 monthly automatic investment for October-December 2026 with a January 2027 resume. Record 9 is the corresponding action item and is paired to i7.
The standing hold Hollis already placed on the joint account - no sales realizing gains until after October 1, 2026, so 2026 gains land on the Tennessee side - is entirely absent from the record.

Missing: Jules to prepare the Ferrant Rollover IRA application and Grevholm distribution form (direct rollover of the vested balance, Graham primary, Theo and Ingrid 50/50 contingent) and send for signature, due Tuesday October 6, 2026 after the date was moved off Friday September 18.

Owner Jules Marchetti is right - the email was reassigned from Hollis because he is away September 21-25. No figures, so nothing to get wrong. Due date is wrong: 'end of next week' from the September 15 meeting is Friday September 25, 2026, but the record encodes 2026-10-27, which also contradicts its own 'by end of next week' task text.

Graham Brennock submitting the Tollefsrud HR work-location change so payroll switches to Tennessee and stops Minnesota withholding. Deadline 'before October 1' is encoded as 2026-10-01, consistent with the agreement, and the task text repeats 'before October 1st'.

Missing: Renata at Venholt benefits enrollment on her first day, Monday October 5, to set the deferral so 2026 stays at the $24,500 limit (~$5,500 of room after roughly $19,000 at Grevholm), override 6% auto-enrollment and ask about a match true-up.
Missing: Renata and Graham to get Tennessee driver's licenses, register to vote in Williamson County and register both cars, within 30 days of October 1 residency, i.e. by end of October 2026.

Jules opening the separate joint house account at Ferrant and sending Graham the title company wire instructions, due Friday October 23, 2026. The date correctly reflects 'a week ahead' of the corrected October 30 closing, not the misheard October 13. No figures stated.

Owner Renata is right and the October-December pause with a January restart is stated accurately; the $2,000 amount is omitted but nothing is misstated. Due date is wrong: Renata committed to doing it in the Ferrant app 'tonight', September 15, 2026; the record's 2026-10-01 is the draft date she was told to beat, not the agreed due date.

extra_items.note: Materially wrong. The Brennocks signed a 12-month lease in Franklin at $4,150 a month and explicitly 'didn't want to buy until we know the area'; a purchase is twelve to eighteen months away and the sale proceeds are being parked in T-bills precisely because no purchase is imminent. No house purchase occurred or was agreed.

Splits the single job-change life event already captured by record 3. The start at Venholt Clinical Logistics on 2026-10-05 is the other half of e1 (leaving Grevholm on September 25 to start at Venholt on October 5); the employer and date are accurate, but it is not a separate event.
